user: And I still have time to file, right?
answer:
It depends on the reason and the charge. Dispute windows run from the transaction date, and today is 15 September 2026 based on your limit data.

| Reason code | Window | TX-0401 (20 Jul, 57 days ago) | TX-0402 (14 Jul, 63 days ago) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Duplicate charge | 60 days | Open, 3 days left | Closed |
| Unauthorised debit | 56 days | Closed | Closed |
| Goods not received | 90 days | Open, 33 days left | Open, 27 days left |
| Service not rendered | 90 days | Open, 33 days left | Open, 27 days left |
| Fraud, card not present | 120 days | Open, 63 days left | Open, 57 days left |

The window is only one condition. Each dispute also needs an eligibility check, and I'll run it once you tell me which charge and what happened. If you think this is a duplicate charge on TX-0401, act within the next 3 days.

Payment dispute rules
## Reason codes and chargeback windows
Each reason code has a window in days from the transaction date. A dispute opened after the window closes is not eligible.

| Reason code | Window (days) |
|---|---|
| fraud_card_not_present | 120 |
| goods_not_received | 90 |
| duplicate_charge | 60 |
| service_not_rendered | 90 |
| unauthorized_debit | 56 |

Glossary
## Chargeback window
The number of days, counted from the transaction date, during which a dispute
may be raised under a given reason code.

Limit operations
## Window definition
Limits are tracked on calendar days, not business days. The daily window runs
from 00:00 to 23:59 CET.

Dispute handling process
## Withdrawing a dispute
A customer may withdraw a dispute at any time before resolution. Withdrawal is
final; the same transaction cannot be disputed again under the same reason code.
